working: Sodium fusion converts sulfur in an organic compound to Na2S (or NaSCN if nitrogen is also present). Na2S gives a coloured complex with sodium nitroprusside. The usual textbook colour is violet/purple; a blood-red colour is more typical of NaSCN with Fe3+. Either way, the test identifies a sulfur-containing amino acid. Methionine, CH3SCH2CH2CH(NH2)COOH, is the only option that contains sulfur. Leucine, threonine and serine have none.
